items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I spoke to him just once... Nat got up from the dais where he was sitting and started toward the band... he just walked past Al and and Billy grabbed my hand and said, 'Man, I certainly enjoyed that.' He say, 'I know you.'

ctx.x: We played a TV show and what made me feel so good, Nat Cole was in town and he didn't play, but he was a guest, you know, and this guy was questioning him. We played out two or three tunes and I had played opposite Nat Cole back in '53, down at the old Blue Note. It was called Lips Low Level then in Chicago. Nat had Charles Norris on bass, John Collins, guitar and Lee Young on drums and himself on piano. We played our set and Nat (unintelligible) would bring his group. I noticed he used to come out and watch us.…

Buster was playing sock cymbal to give us a little leverage, you know, and it seemed like Nat marveled at that. I spoke to him just once -- and like I say, I didn't know of him -- but he remembered me in Philly here in '61 because when we finished the show, they had featured me on the last tune, and I had a little thing I did on Lester Young's "Lester Leaps In," and my solo work, you know. So when I finished, and we were standing there, Nat got up from the dais where he was sitting and started toward the band. So…

to sleep and we had a matinee that Sunday and I didn't make the gig and he said, "I looked for you and you didn't show up that night. What happened?" So that was just one time, but Al Gray teases me now. He says, "Yeah, here's the only cat, Nat Cole walked over and shook his hand instead of my hand and I'm the leader of the band."
